Axiom:
In `add-module` mode the invariant is that the new module must not break its siblings — not a blanket freeze on every sibling file. Default shape: - new `specs///.spec.md`; - scope spec Module Map: APPEND new module row (append at end). Other rows untouched by default; - scope spec Usage Example (ex-Golden DX): rewritten as composition view per `AX_SCOPE_SPEC_MODULE_MAP_OWNERSHIP` (the ONE exception to «other scope-spec sections untouched by default»).
When the new module's own requirement genuinely needs a sibling module to change to fit it — a contract it must call, a Port it must implement against — updating that sibling spec is ordinary work, not a forbidden act: run the `module` flow again in `refine-module` mode for that specific module, in the SAME round this need surfaced. Reaching instead for a parallel mechanism that avoids touching the sibling is the move that needs justifying, not the sibling edit itself (`AX_PARALLEL_MECHANISM_REQUIRES_JUSTIFICATION`). What stays forbidden is an UNREQUIRED sibling edit — touching another module's spec beyond what THIS module's own requirement demands.
